2610.13563.title: Not All Correct Fixes Run Alike: An Empirical Study of Patch Performance in Repository-Level Issue Resolution
2610.13563.paper_summary: Repository-level issue-resolution benchmarks such as SWE-bench evaluate submitted patches primarily based on whether they pass the correctness tests, leaving the runtime performance of different test-passing patches largely unexplored. Evaluating patch performance is essential but challenging since designing performance workloads for each benchmark instance is costly. However, these benchmarks already provide a natural candidate: the built-in \emph{FAIL\_TO\_PASS} (F2P) tests, which exercise the behavior affected by the issue fix. We therefore investigate whether the provided F2P tests can be repurposed to evaluate patch performance. Overall, we choose four frontier models, Claude Opus~5, GPT~5.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen~3.8 Max, paired with SWE-agent to resolve the pre-filtered measurable corpus from verified splits of SWE-bench and SWE-bench-Live, yielding 262 cases with at least two different correct solutions, including the developer ground-truth patch. We then measure each solution's runtime performance in instruction count and wall-clock time on the native F2P test, and use Welch ANOVA instead of the RSD proposed in prior work as a more robust statistical discrimination criterion. We find that this methodology exhibits notable discrimination capability in runtime performance and identifies performance differences among patches in almost half of the instances. Our empirical study shows that the runtime performance of generated patches is independent of the issue resolution rate of LLMs, with nearly reversed model rankings. The case study also shows that the performance analysis reveals architectural regression in some patches that the correctness evaluation overlooked. These findings suggest that resolution rate does not adequately characterize LLMs' capability for repository-level issue resolution, motivating future evaluations to consider patch performance alongside it.
2610.13563.paper_summary_zh: 庫級問題解決基準如SWE-bench主要根據提交的補丁是否通過正確性測試來評估，對於不同通過測試的補丁的運行時性能則大多未被探索。評估補丁性能是必要的，但也具有挑戰性，因為為每個基準實例設計性能工作負載的成本很高。然而，這些基準已經提供了一個自然的候選者：內建的\emph{FAIL\_TO\_PASS} (F2P) 測試，這些測試檢驗了受問題修復影響的行為。因此，我們調查提供的F2P測試是否可以重新用於評估補丁性能。總體而言，我們選擇了四個前沿模型，Claude Opus~5、GPT~5.6、DeepSeek V4 Pro和Qwen~3.8 Max，並與SWE-agent配對，以解決來自經過驗證的SWE-bench和SWE-bench-Live的預過濾可測量語料庫，產生262個案例，這些案例至少有兩個不同的正確解決方案，包括開發者的真實補丁。我們然後在本地F2P測試上測量每個解決方案的運行時性能，包括指令數和實時計時，並使用Welch ANOVA而不是先前工作中提出的RSD作為更穩健的統計區分標準。我們發現這種方法在運行時性能上展現出顯著的區分能力，並在幾乎一半的實例中識別出補丁之間的性能差異。我們的實證研究顯示，生成補丁的運行時性能與LLMs的問題解決率無關，模型排名幾乎是反向的。案例研究還顯示，性能分析揭示了一些補丁的架構回歸，而正確性評估則忽略了這一點。這些發現表明，解決率並不足以充分表徵LLMs在庫級問題解決中的能力，促使未來的評估考慮補丁性能。
